name: Dormant-bud cryopreservation of Malus and Pyrus germplasm: 35 mm single-bud stem sections dehydrated to 30% moisture, cooled at 1 °C/h to -30 °C in a Kryo 360-3.3, held 24 h, stored in LN2 vapour
plain_name: Back up apple and pear tree varieties by slowly freezing their winter buds
description: Fruit Genebank Dresden-Pillnitz (JKI) duplicate-collection method: winter-dormant budwood is cut into 35 mm single-bud sections, dehydrated to 30% moisture at -5 °C, placed in 4.5 mL cryovials, cooled at 1 °C/h to -30 °C in a controlled-rate freezer, held at -30 °C for 24 h, transferred to the vapour phase over liquid nitrogen, and later rewarmed at +4 °C for 24 h before grafting.
keywords: Back up apple and pear tree varieties by slowly freezing their winter buds

sources.citation: Hoefer M, Flachowsky H (2023). Cryopreservation of Malus and Pyrus Wild Species in the 'Fruit Genebank' in Dresden-Pillnitz, Germany. Biology 12(2):200. doi:10.3390/biology12020200

requirements.rationale: The controlled-rate freezer must reach and hold -30 °C (243.15 K) for 24 h.
The slow-cooling rate is 1 °C/h = 16.67 mK/min, which has no exact decimal form in mK/min; the machine's controllable rate range must cover 16-17 mK/min, an interval containing 1 °C/h.
After the -30 °C hold the vials are stored in the vapour phase over liquid nitrogen in a separate Biosafe tank; optional for the freezing machine itself.
A programmed controlled-rate freezer is used; supporting flag only.
Each sample is a 35 mm stem section (two or three per 4.5 mL cryovial); the sample space must accept at least that length. Optional because vial dimensions are not given.

confirmation_note: Requirements taken from the cited procedure and independently re-verified against the source (research/v4, 2026-11-01). Users must confirm them for their own run; edits require confirmation again.
